content.text: Track what I eat and how much, with calories, history and trends.

content.reply:
Got it: a food diary you keep adding to, with per-day calorie totals, full history and trends. Three quick questions below so I get it right the first time.

One honest limit: Alpha can do the calculations today, but saving your entries, showing them in an interface, and estimating calories from a food description aren't connected yet (record storage, the interaction kit, model-based estimates). I'll write the brief as you actually want it, and Alpha builds it the moment those land.

interpretation.outcome: A personal food diary that keeps every meal you log, shows each day's calories, and shows how your intake moves over days and weeks.
interpretation.main_input: Quick entries you make yourself: what you ate, how much, when, and the calories.
interpretation.useful_result: Open it, add a meal in seconds, see today's running total against a daily target, and look back at any past day or a weekly trend.
important_assumptions: Reusable tool, not a one-off file: it keeps a growing history.
Entries are dated and grouped by day, newest first.
It is for you alone, kept on this Mac.
Meals are labelled breakfast, lunch, dinner or snack, and the label can be left blank.

questions.question: Where should the calories come from?
options: Alpha estimates them from what I describe, and I can correct it
Both: estimate, but I can overwrite
questions.why_it_matters: Typing them yourself is straightforward; automatic estimates from a food description need a capability that isn't connected yet.

questions.question: Do you want a daily calorie target to compare against?
options: Yes, and I want to change it over time
questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether each day shows just a total or a total versus a goal, with over/under.

questions.question: Anything besides calories worth tracking?
options: Calories plus protein, carbs and fat
questions.why_it_matters: Adding protein or similar later would mean re-entering past meals, so it's cheaper to decide now.

content.reply:
Clear. A food diary where you type the calories, with one fixed daily target and no extra nutrients. Add a meal in seconds, see today's total and how far over or under you are, open any past day, and watch 7- and 30-day trends. I've dropped the calorie-estimating idea since you're entering the numbers yourself.

The honest limit stays: saving your entries and the diary's own interface aren't connected yet (record storage, the interaction kit). The calculations — daily totals, averages, trends — Alpha can do today. The brief is written as you want it, and Alpha builds it the moment those two land.

interpretation.outcome: A personal food diary on this Mac: log meals with calories, see each day's total against one fixed daily target, browse history and see trends.

interpretation.useful_result: Add a meal in seconds; today's total and over/under the target; any past day on demand; 7- and 30-day trends with averages.
important_assumptions: You type calories yourself, so no estimating is involved.
One fixed daily target applies to every day, and you can change it whenever you like.
Calories only, no protein, carbs or fat.
Days run midnight to midnight, local time.
Amount stays free text like "1 bowl" or "200 g".

content.text: Turn my meeting notes into a one-page brief I can send to my team.

content.reply: Got it — one set of notes in, one shareable brief out. Today I can do this in the conversation: you paste the notes, I return a clean brief with Context, Decisions, Actions (owner and due date) and Next steps, ready to copy into an email. Two limits, straight up: I can't open files from your Mac or save the brief as a document yet, and I can't send it to your team — you'll send it yourself. Rewriting messy prose into polished summary language isn't available yet either, so I work from the structure your notes already have. Three quick questions first.

interpretation.outcome: Turn a set of meeting notes into a short, clean one-page brief you can share with your team.
interpretation.main_input: The meeting notes themselves, pasted into the conversation.
interpretation.useful_result: A tidy brief with context, key decisions, action items with owners, and next steps — short enough to fit on one page.
important_assumptions: You paste the notes here; Alpha cannot open files from your Mac yet.
The brief comes back as text in the conversation, ready to copy into your email or doc.
Structuring works from cues already in your notes (bullets, names, words like 'decision', 'action', 'due').
Default sections: Context, Decisions, Actions (owner + due), Next steps.
Roughly 400 words or less, so it prints to one page.
Nothing is stored after the brief is produced.

questions.question: Is this a one-off, or do you want the same brief after every meeting?
questions.why_it_matters: A one-off is a single transformation; every meeting means a reusable tool worth building properly.

questions.question: Which sections must the brief have?
questions.why_it_matters: It decides what gets kept and what gets dropped to fit one page.

questions.question: Should action items be pulled into a list with owner and due date?
options: Yes, with owner and due date
questions.why_it_matters: Owners and dates only appear if your notes name them; otherwise I flag them as unassigned.

content.text: Every morning, send my mom a WhatsApp message with today's weather for Ahmedabad.

content.reply: I can plan this, but I'll be straight with you: three pieces are missing today. Alpha can't send WhatsApp messages (no messaging service is connected, and it isn't planned for the first release), can't read live weather from the web yet, and can't run itself on a morning schedule yet. So there's no useful partial version I can hand you now. I've written the brief for exactly what you asked, and Alpha will build it once those arrive. Two quick things so it's ready to go: what time should it send, and what should the message say?

interpretation.outcome: A small daily helper that checks today's Ahmedabad weather each morning and sends your mom a short WhatsApp message about it.
interpretation.main_input: A live weather source for Ahmedabad, plus your mom's WhatsApp number.
interpretation.useful_result: One friendly message in her chat each morning: today's high and low, conditions, and a rain warning if rain is likely.
important_assumptions: Recurring, so this is a reusable solution rather than a one-off message.
Temperatures in Celsius, times in India Standard Time.
One message per day; it skips rather than double-sends if today is already done.
Short plain-text message in English by default.

questions.why_it_matters: Sets the daily schedule and how early the forecast is fetched.

options: Add a rain or heat warning when relevant
Add a short caring line, e.g. 'carry an umbrella'

questions.question: Which WhatsApp number should it send to, and in English or Gujarati?
questions.why_it_matters: The recipient and language are needed before it can ever send.
